Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be an
oriented link with $r\ge1$ components and complement $X_L$,
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]), and let
$$\varphi:H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z$$
be the **total linking homomorphism**, defined as the composite
$$H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\mathrm{Alex}}\widetilde H^1(L;\mathbb Z)\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^rH^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\text{sum}}\mathbb Z,$$
where the first arrow is Alexander duality
([[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]),
each $H^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is the orientation-induced
identification, and the last map sums the $r$ coordinates. By
[[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]] the map $\varphi$
may again be written $\pi_1(X_L)\to H_1(X_L)\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathbb Z$; we
denote both composites by $\varphi$ and set $K:=\ker\varphi$.

The **one-variable Alexander module** of $L$ is
$$A_L:=H_1(\widetilde{X_L};\mathbb Z),$$
the first singular homology of the connected infinite cyclic cover
$p:\widetilde{X_L}\to X_L$ classified by $K$
([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]],
[[lem-subgroup-quotient-of-universal-cover]],
[[def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods]]), equipped with its
structure of module over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) in which $t$ acts by the deck
transformation corresponding to the positive generator of
$\operatorname{Deck}(\widetilde{X_L}/X_L)\cong\mathbb Z$.

**Caveats.** The cover is the one classified by $K=\ker\varphi$; since $K$ is
normal the cover is regular and its deck group is
$\pi_1(X_L)/K\cong\mathbb Z$
([[def-regular-covering]], [[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]], [[cor-deck-group-of-a-regular-covering]],
[[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]]). The module $A_L$ is ordinary
integral homology of the cover, with the deck action as its module structure;
no twisting by a representation of the link group is used. The total linking
homomorphism satisfies $\varphi(\mu_i)=1$ for a meridian $\mu_i$ of any one
component, so $r\ge1$ is needed for $\varphi$ to be interesting and $A_L$
depends on the orientations of all components through this map.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be the ordered integral basis and positive normal push-off convention used to define the Seifert matrix $V$ above. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. For such representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between the positive push-off of $x$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off, and equals the bilinear extension of $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The linking number of two disjoint oriented circle components is symmetric. In particular, the Seifert pairing is a well-defined bilinear map $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$.

Assume full AC. In oriented $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$, fix $R>2r>0$ and $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. Let $M_\epsilon$ be the embedded Möbius band parametrized by
$$m(\theta,t)=((R+t\cos(\theta/2))\cos\theta,(R+t\cos(\theta/2))\sin\theta,-\epsilon t\sin(\theta/2)),\qquad |t|\le r,$$
with $(0,t)$ identified with $(2\pi,-t)$. Its core is oriented by increasing $\theta$. Its boundary is an unknot, its integral normal-transfer pairing is $[\epsilon]$ on the core generator, and its boundary normal framing has self-linking $2\epsilon$.

Let $F$ be any connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary and a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. Form $F'$ as the separated boundary connected sum of $F$ with a small copy of $M_\epsilon$: the two surfaces lie in disjoint ball interiors, joined along chosen boundary arcs by an untwisted product band whose interior misses them, and whose normal collar is the product of the chosen boundary normal collars. Smooth the seams. Then the boundary link of $F'$ is ambient isotopic to that of $F$, its normal pairing is integrally congruent to $B_F\oplus[\epsilon]$, and its boundary normal Euler quantity satisfies $e(F')=e(F)-2\epsilon$, where $e(S)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$ for componentwise normal push-offs determined by its surface collar. Consequently
$$\operatorname{sign}(B_{F'})+\tfrac12e(F')=\operatorname{sign}(B_F)+\tfrac12e(F).$$
Neither surface is required to be orientable, and the boundary link may have any positive number of components.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary, possibly nonorientable, with a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. The ambient three-sphere has its standard orientation. For oriented integral multicurves $a,b\subset\operatorname{int}F$, let $\tau b$ be the cycle consisting of the two small normal pushes over $b$, oriented by projection to $b$. For a one-sided circle this is one circle mapping with degree two, rather than a choice of a single normal direction. Then
$B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a well-defined symmetric integral bilinear pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, independently of representatives and sufficiently small normal pushes. Every integral homology class has an oriented multicurve representative, permitting integer coefficients. The pairing extends to rational homology, with quadratic form $q_F(x)=B_F(x,x)$ satisfying the normal-transfer linking identity.

For an embedded compact subsurface $A\subset F$ with such a finite presentation, the pairing on $A$ is the pullback of $B_F$ under inclusion. If $F$ is oriented and its boundary is one knot, its pairing has matrix $V+V^T$ in any integral basis, where $V$ is the positive-push Seifert matrix. Orientation-preserving ambient isotopies transport the pairing.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $X$ be a nonempty
compact connected one-dimensional topological manifold without boundary
([[def-compact-space]], [[def-connected-space]],
[[def-hausdorff-space]]). Then $X$ is homeomorphic to the circle
$S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$
([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]). If in addition $X$ carries a
smooth structure making it a smooth one-manifold without boundary, then $X$ is
diffeomorphic to this circle
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]).

The empty manifold is excluded by the hypothesis: it is compact and connected
under the conventions of this library, but it is not homeomorphic to a circle.
The hypothesis "without boundary" is likewise essential: the closed interval
$[0,1]$ is compact and connected but has boundary points and is not a circle.

derivations.claim: Choose a small normal push $K_i'$ disjoint from the whole surface $F$. Triangulate its finite disk-and-band presentation and choose arbitrary reference orientations on its finitely many triangles. Their sum modulo two is a fundamental two-chain with boundary the sum of the boundary circles modulo two. Lift that two-chain to an integral chain $C$ in $S^3\setminus K_i'$ by using the chosen triangle orientations, and orient the boundary circles as prescribed in the Statement. Then $\partial C-\sum_j K_j=2z$ for an integral one-chain $z$. Its boundary is zero, because $2\partial z=0$ and singular chain groups have no integer torsion. Applying the linking homomorphism with $K_i'$ from [F1] gives $0=\sum_j\operatorname{lk}(K_i',K_j)+2\operatorname{lk}(K_i',z)$. This use on $z$ is on complement homology and does not require it to be embedded. For $j\ne i$ the small push is homotopic to $K_i$ in the complement of $K_j$. The $i$th term is $f_i(F)$ by symmetry. Reduction modulo two proves the stated parity formula, independently of the orientability of $F$.

A smooth boundary circle has an oriented normal disk bundle with a smooth trivialization. One may construct it on a cut parameter interval using finitely many normal frames, then correct the endpoint rotation by a smooth angle interpolation so that the frames glue; the oriented two-plane rotation group is connected. The normal exponential chart is injective at a sufficiently small uniform radius by [F4] and compactness, as in the normal-transfer construction. In these coordinates a nowhere-zero transverse vector along the circle has an angular lift on the cut interval, whose endpoint difference is $2\pi$ times an integer. Its small pushed curve is a longitude plus that many positive meridians. By [F1] its self-linking is the self-linking of the reference longitude plus this integer. In particular two such fields have the same self-linking precisely when their angular lifts differ by a periodic smooth function. Surface inward conormals and surface normals along an oriented boundary circle differ by a fixed quarter-turn in its oriented normal plane. They therefore have the same integer and the same self-linking. These assertions concern boundary collars only and do not orient the whole surface.

By step 1.1 the difference $d_i=f_i(F_1)-f_i(F_0)$ is even. If $d_i\ne0$, add $|d_i|/2$ crosscaps of sign $\epsilon=\operatorname{sign}(d_i)$ to that component of $F_0$, using [F2]. Each increases that component's self-linking by $2\epsilon$: the total Euler change is $-2\epsilon$, and the other component self-linkings are unchanged. Such a small separated attachment is available in a boundary chart, placing its Möbius band in a small ball off the surface and joining through a product collar of the chosen boundary arc. After each attachment use the local boundary-link isotopy in [F2] to return the boundary to the original $L$; linking and framings are transported by that isotopy. Use disjoint small boundary neighborhoods for the finitely many required attachments, or successive smaller neighborhoods. Connectedness and the finite disk-and-band presentation are retained. This produces a surface $\widehat F_0$ whose component framings equal those of $F_1$.

Work in disjoint sufficiently short normal tubes of the boundary circles, containing no other parts of either surface than their boundary collars. Choose the tube coordinates adapted to the actual collar of $F_1$, so it is the radial ray of angle zero. Explicitly extend its collar parametrization $c(s,x)$ slightly across $x=0$, and map $(s,x,y)$ to the short ambient normal push by $y$ of $c(s,x)$. The boundary-circle tangent, the inward collar vector and its ambient normal are independent, so [F4] gives this chart at $x=y=0$, and compactness gives a uniform tube. The finite boundary-chart extensions agree on the prescribed collar and can be patched beyond its boundary before shrinking. Thus the whole collar, rather than only its tangent line, is the angle-zero ray. On a short collar of $\widehat F_0$, the base projection to the boundary circle is a coordinate and the normal radius is a strictly increasing inward parameter. This follows at the boundary from the nonzero inward transverse derivative, then uniformly by compactness and [F4]. Thus its collar has coordinates $(s,r,\theta(s,r))$, with its angular direction tending to a smooth angle field at $r=0$. Its relative angular winding is zero by steps 1.2 and 2.1. It therefore has a periodic real angular lift on a sufficiently short collar. First straighten its angle to its limiting field on a smaller radius strip, using an angular interpolation cut off before the outer edge; then interpolate that limiting field to a fixed small angle $\delta\ne0$, again cut off in radius. Throughout these interpolations the base coordinate $s$ and radius $r$ are unchanged, so distinct parameters remain distinct and the collar stays embedded even if the angle varies in $r$. The formulas extend smoothly across $r=0$: they are rotations of the smooth transverse vector by a periodic smooth angle, while the initial straightening error vanishes with $r$. All changes vanish on an outer collar. The final innermost collar is the ray of angle $\delta$ and is disjoint from the angle-zero interior collar of $F_1$.

Extend the collar embedding isotopies of step 3.1 by the unchanged embedding on the remainder of $\widehat F_0$ and use [F5]. The ambient extension fixes every boundary point because the embedding isotopy fixes it; no claim that this extension fixes the comparison surface is needed. Perform it on the finitely many disjoint boundary tubes. Denote the endpoint by $F_0'$. It still has boundary $L$, retains its component framings by [F3], and misses $F_1$ in a punctured neighborhood of each boundary component. Shrink to a common such neighborhood $U$. The given finite smooth presentation is transported by the isotopies.

It remains to make the intersection outside $U$ transverse. In the boundaryless ambient manifold $S^3\setminus L$, the target $F_1\setminus L$ is a closed embedded boundaryless surface. All possible intersections of the two surfaces are contained in a compact region outside a smaller $U$. In finitely many ambient charts covering that region choose three bump-supported vector fields spanning each tangent space on smaller covering charts, with supports away from a still smaller neighborhood of $L$. Compose their short flows with parameters $a_j$, obtaining ambient diffeomorphisms $h_a$ fixed there. At zero parameter the parameter derivatives span the ambient tangent space on every possible intersection. For a sufficiently small parameter ball the same remains true at all intersections, by compactness and continuity; regions outside those covering charts retain their positive separation or are fixed. Thus the evaluation $(x,a)\mapsto h_a(x)$ from the interior of $F_0'$ is transverse to $F_1\setminus L$. Apply [F6] and choose an arbitrarily small good parameter. The path of short flows from zero to it is an ambient isotopy fixed near $L$. Its endpoint $F_0^*$ is transverse to the comparison surface outside $L$ and retains the separated collars.

Their interior intersection is now a compact one-dimensional smooth manifold with no boundary: it is transverse away from $L$ and absent in a punctured neighborhood of $L$. Compactness gives a finite cover by connected interval charts, so there are finitely many components. Each component is closed and hence compact, and [F7] makes it a smooth embedded circle. Thus only finitely many interior circles remain. Every crosscap move preserved the corrected signature by [F2], and every subsequent ambient isotopy preserved both its pairing signature and all component self-linkings by [F1] and [F3]. Their finite composition therefore preserves $\operatorname{sign}(B)+e/2$. The component labels and chosen orientations were transported throughout. This proves the claimed normalization while leaving the remaining entire-surface comparison as a separate obligation.

boundaries.evidence: Step 6.1 allows the final circle family to be empty.
Step 2.1 adds no crosscap when the framing difference is zero.
Steps 1.1–2.1 apply to a single link component and an even difference of magnitude two.

boundaries.reason: Smooth embedded surfaces and a finite smooth disk-and-band presentation are supplied; normal collar derivatives are nonzero.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 3.1–4.1 fix the boundary circles pointwise while separating their actual interior collars; step5.1 is fixed near the link.
Step 5.1 explicitly invokes full AC through countable-choice parametric transversality; all selected charts, frames and crosscaps are finite.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from normal-transfer linking, componentwise positive-meridian linking and the explicit crosscap supplier. It implies countable choice for supported isotopy extension and parametric transversality.

risk_review.notes: Parity proof lifts the mod2fundamental chain to an integral chain and avoids an unproved mod2linking comparison. Collar isotopies preserve base and radius with periodic angular lifts; final transversality uses a finite ambient-flow family. General surface S*equivalence is not claimed.

lem-spanning-surfaces-can-match-boundary.proof_status_evidence: Seven literal steps and scoped successful precheck/render/layout; independent owner mathematical reading remains owed.
